events.description: Rumsfeld announces drawdown of about half a brigade from Afghanistan.
Zakir transferred from Guantanamo to Afghanistan in late 2007.
Afghan government releases Zakir; named Taliban leader in Helmand.
Biden dines with Karzai in Afghanistan and storms out.
Biden in Baghdad thanks Obama for ending the war.
US Rangers and Afghan forces raid Shorabak al-Qaeda training camp.
McMaster visits Afghanistan and meets Ghani.
Trump announces Afghanistan strategy relying on Afghan forces, more advisors and air support.
McMaster and Bowman publish WSJ essay listing six steps to avoid disaster.
US withdrawal and Taliban takeover; Islamic Emirate re-established.
Al-Qaeda leader killed in Kabul while sheltered by Sirajuddin Haqqani and the Taliban interior ministry.
Taliban announce Zakir as military commander in Panjshir.
Chaotic US evacuation from Kabul airport, which McMaster says was made worse by closing Bagram under the troop cap.
McMaster and Brad Bowman publish a Wall Street Journal essay listing six steps needed to avoid disaster in Afghanistan, including intensified air support and keeping Bagram open.
Biden sets a 2,500-troop cap and a withdrawal deadline around September 1 (originally September 11).

key_claims: Al-Qaeda never left Afghanistan; its leader was killed in Kabul while sheltered by Sirajuddin Haqqani, the Taliban deputy emir and interior minister.
There is no moderate Taliban; the Taliban government is dominated by the old guard.
The Haqqani Network and al-Qaeda are so intertwined that Sirajuddin Haqqani is described as essentially al-Qaeda.
Ex-Gitmo detainee Abdul Qayyum Zakir became Taliban military chief and is now a deputy defense minister and Panjshir commander.
McMaster says Trump's August 2017 strategy was working, with advisors embedded lower and Taliban-held territory plateauing, before talks and the timeline undermined it.
The US negotiated with the Taliban while announcing withdrawal and ceasing to target them, which the hosts say led to the Doha deal and the collapse.
Al-Qaeda now has both a safe haven and state sponsorship, which the hosts see as worse than pre-9/11.
Pakistan's ISI is accused of continued support for the Taliban and of manipulating Karzai, and US aid to Pakistan is criticized as serial gullibility.
McMaster argues that a 2,500-troop cap made keeping Bagram open impossible and forced a risky evacuation from Kabul airport.
McMaster says political leadership must be held accountable, though some blame also lies with the generals.
He says the Biden administration did not adopt the six steps he and Brad Bowman recommended.
McMaster says the humanitarian catastrophe in Afghanistan is caused by the Taliban, and that aid only props them up.
The hosts and McMaster argue the US should consider supporting Afghan resistance groups to remove the Taliban.
